prŏpīnātĭo , ōnis, f. propino.
I. A drinking to one's health, a pledging in something (post-Aug.): “tralaticiā propinatione dignus,” Petr. 113 : “propinationem ab aliquo accipere,” Sen. Ben. 2, 21, 5 .—In plur.: “propinationibus crebris aliquem lacessere,” Sen. Ira, 2, 33, 6 : propinationes tuas recusant, decline your invitations to drink a
health, id. Ep. 83, 22.—
II. Transf., in gen., a funeral banquet, Inscr. Grut. 753, 4.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
